events.title: Battle of Otumba
events.description: Spanish conquistadors led by Hernán Cortés, fleeing Tenochtitlan after the Noche Triste, defeated a much larger Aztec force at Otumba. The Spanish were exhausted and heavily outnumbered.
events.significance: The victory let Cortés's battered army reach safety and regroup. They returned to besiege and capture the Aztec capital the following year.

events.title: Hawaii Annexed by the United States
events.description: President William McKinley signed the Newlands Resolution. It annexed the Republic of Hawaii as a U.S. territory during the Spanish-American War.
events.significance: The annexation extended American power deep into the Pacific. Hawaii became a state in 1959.

events.title: Death of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle
events.description: The British author who created Sherlock Holmes died at his home in Sussex, England, at age 71.
events.significance: Holmes and Dr. Watson shaped detective fiction, and the genre still follows the template they set.

events.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident
events.description: Chinese and Japanese troops clashed near the Marco Polo Bridge outside Beijing. The skirmish led to full-scale fighting.
events.significance: The clash marked the start of the Second Sino-Japanese War. That war later merged into World War II in Asia.

events.title: London Bombings
events.description: Four suicide bombers attacked London's public transport system during the morning rush hour, killing 52 people and injuring hundreds.
events.significance: It was the deadliest terrorist attack in the United Kingdom since 1988. It led to major changes in British security and counter-terrorism policy.
